news.headline: Alphabet Joins Dow Jones on June 29, Replacing Verizon After 22 Years
news.body: Alphabet (GOOGL) officially replaced Verizon (VZ) in the 30-stock Dow Jones Industrial Average at the open on June 29, 2026, the first Dow change since November 2024. With Verizon's share price (~$45) accounting for only ~0.5% of the price-weighted index, S&P Dow Jones Indices cited Alphabet's higher share price (~$350) and diversified portfolio spanning AI, cloud, advertising, and healthcare tech as rationale. All five of the largest U.S. tech firms — Nvidia, Amazon, Apple, Microsoft, and Alphabet — now hold Dow seats, deepening the benchmark's AI-trade exposure. The swap forced Dow-tracking funds such as SPDR DIA to sell VZ and buy GOOGL ahead of the open, with Alphabet having gained ~1% and Verizon falling ~2% on the initial announcement.

news.headline: Russell Indexes Go Live With First-Ever Semi-Annual Reconstitution on June 29
news.body: The newly reconstituted Russell US Indexes took effect at the open of U.S. markets on Monday, June 29, marking the first semi-annual rebalancing after FTSE Russell shifted from an annual to a twice-yearly schedule in 2026. The Nasdaq Closing Cross set a record on June 26, executing $334 billion in Nasdaq-listed securities in 1.63 seconds to complete the reshuffle. The total market cap of the Russell 3000 surged 29% year-over-year to $75.6 trillion, with the large/small-cap breakpoint rising 24% to $5.7 billion. Markets are watching for post-recon flow reversals and fresh passive-fund positioning as the reconstituted indexes debut on Monday.

news.headline: Seagate (STX) Slides 18% From Peak as AI Capex Fears Trigger Storage Selloff
news.body: Seagate Technology shares have retreated roughly 18% from their $1,055 all-time high, closing at $899.90 on June 26 after a 12.24% single-session drop, with continued weakness into June 28-29. The initial trigger was a report that South Korea's SK Hynix is slowing its HBM4 high-bandwidth memory expansion, which rattled the broader AI infrastructure complex and dragged storage names including Western Digital and SanDisk lower alongside STX. Additional headwinds included a Fox Advisors downgrade to Equal-Weight on June 22 and rising Fed rate-hike odds under Chair Kevin Warsh, which pressure debt-funded AI capex. Markets are watching the move closely given STX is still up over 230% year-to-date, with next real fundamental test at fiscal Q4 2026 earnings expected in late July.

news.headline: S&P 500 Futures Jump as US-Iran Halt Attacks Ahead of Doha Peace Talks
news.body: U.S. equity futures climbed Monday after Washington and Tehran agreed to halt attacks against each other before peace negotiations resume in Doha. S&P 500 futures rose roughly 0.58% and Nasdaq futures gained 0.85% in pre-market trading on June 29. The geopolitical relief follows a turbulent week in which Iran targeted a container ship and military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, triggering retaliatory U.S. strikes. Markets are treating the renewed ceasefire as a buying catalyst heading into the second half of 2026, with the S&P 500 down roughly 3% in June after strong April-May gains.

news.headline: SpaceX (SPCX) to Join Nasdaq-100 on July 7, Triggering Billions in Forced Buying
news.body: Nasdaq confirmed on June 26–27 that SpaceX (SPCX) will enter the Nasdaq-100 Index before market open on July 7, 2026 — the fastest-ever index inclusion, just 15 trading days post-IPO, enabled by a new Nasdaq fast-track rule. Analysts estimate passive funds tracking the benchmark must purchase up to $7.3 billion in SPCX shares as part of mandatory rebalancing. The stock, which had retreated ~32% from its post-IPO peak of $225.64 to around $153, recovered modestly on the news. The inclusion underscores institutional demand but raises valuation questions given SPCX's negative earnings and P/S ratio near 79x.

news.headline: SoftBank Breaks Below ¥6,000 as OpenAI IPO Delay Pressure Persists Into Monday
news.body: SoftBank Group (TSE: 9984) fell below the ¥6,000 level during Asian trading on June 29, extending the prior session's 12.5% collapse triggered by NYT reports that OpenAI is leaning toward delaying its IPO to 2027 rather than accept a valuation below $1 trillion. SoftBank holds approximately a 13% stake in OpenAI worth a cumulative ~$65 billion, and a $40 billion bridge loan taken to fund the investment is due for repayment in March 2027 with no public exit now in sight. Technical analysts flagged the ¥4,800–5,000 zone as next key support. The two-day rout has wiped roughly ¥5.6 trillion in market cap and weighed heavily on the broader Nikkei 225.

news.headline: KOSPI Falls 3%, Samsung Down 5.3% as Korea Exchange Scraps Weekly Options Launch
news.body: South Korea's KOSPI slid ~3% to around 8,154 on June 29 as Samsung Electronics dropped 5.3% and SK Hynix fell 3.4%, with stocks failing to react positively to a combined ₩2,000 trillion ($1.3 trillion) chip investment pledge by Samsung Group and SK Group presented to President Lee Jae-myung. The Korea Exchange's Financial Supervisory Service indefinitely postponed the planned June 29 launch of weekly single-stock options on Samsung, SK Hynix, Hyundai Motor, and LG Energy Solution, citing record-high volatility fuelled by retail investors piling into daily 2x leveraged ETFs. The regulatory pullback removed a key hedging tool and compounded bearish sentiment following a circuit-breaker week. KOSPI is now down roughly 10% over the past week, erasing ~₩550 trillion in market cap.

news.headline: Nikkei Posts Biggest Single-Day Point Drop of 2026, Closing Down 4.15% on June 27
news.body: Japan's Nikkei 225 plunged 3,005 points (−4.15%) to close at 69,361 on June 27, its largest single-session decline this year and third-largest on record by points, as SoftBank's 12.9% collapse on OpenAI IPO delay reports dragged AI-adjacent heavyweights across the board. Kioxia Holdings slid 11.2%, while Advantest, Tokyo Electron, and Fujikura also saw heavy selling; TSE Prime Market turnover surged to ¥12.17 trillion (~$75.2 billion). The close broke below the psychologically key 70,000 level that the index had consolidated above for much of June. Notably, advancing issues still outnumbered decliners 915 to 613, indicating the rout was concentrated in index heavyweights rather than a broad market panic.

news.headline: Kioxia Plans US Depositary Share Offering Spring 2027 and Domestic Stock Split
news.body: Japan's Kioxia Holdings (TSE: 285A) announced on June 25 plans to offer US depositary shares in spring 2027 and execute a domestic stock split, capitalising on AI-driven demand for NAND flash exposure to broaden its global investor base alongside rival SK Hynix. Kioxia has grown into Japan's most valuable listed company in 2026 on the back of AI data-centre storage demand, and guided operating profit of ~¥1.3 trillion for Q1 FY2026. The announcement came just ahead of the broader AI tech selloff; Kioxia shares subsequently slid 12% on June 26 and broke below ¥90,000 by June 29 as the sector correction deepened. The US listing plan nonetheless underscores the continued global capital-raising ambitions of Asian memory chipmakers.

news.headline: WTI Rebounds to ~$70 as US-Iran Agree Ceasefire; Hormuz Shipping at 75% of Pre-War Levels
news.body: Crude oil recovered to around $70/bbl on June 29 after sinking to four-month lows near $69 on Friday following a surge in Strait of Hormuz shipping transits. Persian Gulf exports have recovered to roughly 75% of pre-war levels, with Saudi Arabia resuming tanker loadings at Ras Tanura and the UAE, Kuwait, and Qatar all ramping output. A US-Iran halt to mutual attacks was agreed ahead of Doha peace talks scheduled for Tuesday, though shipowners remain cautious with hundreds of vessels still stranded in the Persian Gulf. WTI has lost over 22% in the past four weeks as the geopolitical risk premium rapidly unwinds.

news.headline: Gold Slips to ~$4,050 as US-Iran De-escalation Revives Inflation and Rate-Hike Fears
news.body: Gold fell to around $4,050/oz on Monday, snapping a two-day rebound, as renewed tit-for-tat US-Iran strikes over the Strait of Hormuz lifted oil prices and re-ignited inflation concerns. Iran targeted a container ship and a vessel carrying Qatari oil, prompting multiple US retaliatory strikes before both sides agreed to suspend attacks ahead of Doha peace talks. In-line May PCE data allowed investors to modestly pare Fed rate-hike bets, offering brief support; gold remains down roughly 3% for its fourth consecutive weekly decline as markets now price three Fed hikes this year with a ~62% probability of the first in September. Silver futures fell 1.7% in tandem, hovering near $58.

news.headline: US Navy Widens Hormuz Transit Corridor, Challenging Iran's Chokehold on Waterway
news.body: On June 27, the US Navy's Joint Maritime Information Center announced a widened navigational route through the Strait of Hormuz near Oman, permitting increased naval and commercial traffic in both directions — a direct challenge to Iran's control over the waterway. The move follows weeks in which ships were trickling out via an Iranian-run vetting lane or slipping through a southern Oman passage with transponders off under US military guidance. Market participants are watching closely as the transit corridor development is the most significant operational shift yet, potentially accelerating the return of the roughly 20 million barrels of oil per day that historically flowed through the strait. Shipping insurers remain cautious pending mine clearance confirmation.

news.headline: Gold Posts Fourth Straight Weekly Loss; PCE In-Line but Fed Hike Bets Remain Elevated
news.body: Gold traded around $4,040/oz on Friday June 27, edging up for a second session after May PCE inflation came in broadly in line with expectations, nudging investors to modestly scale back rate-hike bets. Despite the bounce, gold closed the week down roughly 3%, its fourth consecutive weekly decline, as Fed Chair Warsh reaffirmed the commitment to price stability and the Fed raised its 2026 PCE inflation projections — headline PCE accelerated to 4.1% in May. Markets remain priced for three Fed hikes this year with markets and major banks including Deutsche Bank warning that three to four hikes could drag gold toward $3,800/oz. The PCE print provides only limited relief ahead of the June jobs report and ISM PMI due this week.

news.headline: US Natural Gas Rises 2%+ on Heat Forecasts; Record Golden Pass LNG Feedgas Lifts Export Flows
news.body: US Henry Hub natural gas futures rose more than 2% to around $3.29–$3.35/MMBtu during the June 27–28 period, hitting their highest level since early February, as forecasters flagged above-average temperatures across the Midwest and Northeast through July 5 that are set to boost gas-for-power demand. Record feedgas activity at the Golden Pass LNG terminal in Texas lifted average daily flows to major export plants to 17.3 bcfd in June from 17.1 bcfd in May. An EIA storage injection of 76 bcf for the week ended June 19 — near the seasonal norm — kept inventories 5.7% above seasonal norms, tempering further upside. LNG export demand combined with hotter summer weather is the primary price driver as US domestic production holds steady near 109–112 bcfd.
